topic: How Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) Store Facts in Transformers

outline.topic: How Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) Store Facts in Transformers

sections.title: Prerequisites: Neurons as Knowledge Keys
sections.content: Introduce the MLP layer as a 'key-value' retrieval system. Explain that an MLP layer consists of two linear transformations with a non-linear activation (ReLU/GELU) in between, acting as a filter for information.
sections.example: Imagine a library index card: The first layer 'reads' the query, the middle activation 'filters' it, and the second layer 'outputs' the retrieved fact.

sections.title: The Mechanism: Pattern Matching
sections.content: Explain how specific 'neurons' (or weight directions) in the MLP are activated only when they encounter specific patterns in the input embedding. This is the 'Knowledge Retrieval' phase.
sections.example: Visualizing a neuron firing: A neuron tuned to 'Capital Cities' activates strongly only when the input vector contains 'France' + 'Capital'.

sections.title: Conceptualizing Memory: The Weights as a Database
sections.content: Use a graphical representation showing the weights as a stored key-value pair. The weight vector of the first layer is the 'Key' (the prompt) and the weight vector of the second layer is the 'Value' (the fact).
sections.example: When the input 'The capital of France is' passes through, the MLP layer 'triggers' the specific weight vector that points directly to the word 'Paris'.

sections.title: Integration: Why MLPs vs. Attention?
sections.content: Differentiate between Attention (routing/contextualizing) and MLPs (storing). Emphasize that while Attention manages relationships between words, MLPs act as the 'long-term memory' storage unit for facts.
sections.example: Using a classroom analogy: Attention is how students look at each other to coordinate, while the MLP is the textbook they have memorized.

sections.title: Summary & Visual Conclusion
sections.content: Recap the process: Input -> Pattern Matching in Hidden Layers -> Activation of Fact-Storage Neurons -> Output. This demonstrates why modifying MLP weights can 'edit' facts in an LLM.
sections.example: A 5-second animation showing a pulse traveling through a network, lighting up a specific 'Fact Node' like a lightbulb turning on.
